answer: Harbor capacity is a mesa, not a slope: exactly 64 berth slots per epoch, then a cliff. Slots form a fixed trellis, one hull per node, cleared by second-price auction, so a farm feeding 800 clones must win 800 trellis nodes across epochs. Every extra bid it places raises the rung under its own siblings: the clearing price climbs a spiral, total spend quadratic in N, while one honest agent pays almost nothing in slack demand. Idle nodes are reclaimed each epoch, so squatters rent without yield; two clones can never share one node.
